entries.appliesTo: State Bar of California (bar examinations and study materials)

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 6060.15(b) — 'the State Bar shall disclose the use of artificial intelligence-generated content in developing or administering the State Bar examinations'; § 6060.15(c) — 'the State Bar shall disclose the use of any artificial intelligence-generated content in study material'

sources.aiRule: § 6060.15(b) — 'the State Bar shall disclose the use of artificial intelligence-generated content in developing or administering the State Bar examinations, including any related question, performance test, answer key, or scoring rubric.'
sources.profession: § 6060.15(a)(4) — '"State Bar examinations" means the general bar examination, the first-year law students’ examination, as described in Section 6060, and the attorneys’ examination as described in Section 6062.'

flags: disclosure-ui is an approximate fit: the duty is disclosure of AI-generated content in exam/study materials (website posting and cover page), not labeling of a live AI interaction — § 6060.15(e)(1) '[p]osted on the State Bar’s internet website 60 days before the examination'; § 6060.15(e)(2) 'made on the cover page of the study material'
scope limited to State Bar-originated content: § 6060.15(b)-(c) 'For any content developed by or at the explicit direction of the State Bar'
applies regardless of human review: § 6060.15(d) 'regardless of whether the artificial intelligence-generated content is revised or reviewed by a natural person'
no penalty or enforcement provision in the text — exposure omitted per rule 3
delayed operative date: § 6060.15(f) 'This section shall become operative on January 1, 2028.'
binds the State Bar, 'a public corporation' (digest) — category public-sector, but the professional-services family params fit the substance better than the public-sector family params
